disclaimer: A watch index for UK type shortages and fuel stress. Individual scores come first. The overall is a blend and does not cancel a bad harvest. It does not see supermarket shelves, and it is not a prediction that a shop will be empty.

food.why: this harvest is the loud food score: wheat yields 11% below the five-year average after a dry spring and summer. Agadir is drier than its usual autumn. wheat futures are down 14% in 30 days. the overall does not cancel that. Shelves can still be stocked while the crop was short.

fuel.why: diesel is 199p and petrol 174p, week of 2026-10-26. diesel is at the 99th percentile of pump prices since 2018. Brent is $111, +8% in 30 days. Dutch gas is 97, +39% in 30 days. Stocks and spare capacity are scored separately and do not cancel this.

spare.why: white diesel in the depot covers about 17 days of the latest month's deliveries. the tightest power day still has 6.6 GW spare. these scores are not the pump price, and a calm spare reading does not make diesel cheap.

parts.name: This harvest
parts.detail: AHDB final 2026 survey: wheat 6.9 t/ha, 11% below the five-year average. Spring barley 17% below, oats 14% below. Oilseed rape was 19% above. They put it down to limited rain from spring onwards, with huge farm-to-farm gaps. Defra's England wheat tonnage is 10.8 million tonnes, 0.8% above 2025, but East of England and South East yields fell. Up on last year is not the same as a normal crop. Full UK figures are due 10 December 2026.

parts.name: Pump prices

parts.name: Oil and gas prices

parts.name: Emergency oil stocks
parts.detail: DESNZ stocks at end of July 2026 [provisional]: 9.6 million tonnes in total, 8.7 million tonnes physically in the UK. That is -10% on the same month a year earlier. Against the last ten years of months, this total sits around the 17th percentile. The last quarterly note said end-June stocks still more than met the IEA 90-day net-import rule. That rule is not the same as fuel in the depot. July deliveries imply about 17 days of white diesel, 24 days of petrol and 26 days of jet fuel.

parts.name: Fuel in the depot
parts.detail: Days of petrol, diesel and jet implied by the latest month of deliveries. This is working stock, not the IEA reserve.

parts.name: Gas in store
parts.detail: National Gas, 28/10/2026: medium-range storage 12,920 (68%). Long-range is published at 0 (0%), so it is not a buffer. LNG tanks held 7,986 GWh at 28/10/2026 15:00. Today's gas demand forecast is 191.0 million cubic metres, against a margins-notice trigger of 464.0. No notice is in force. Storage cannot carry a normal day on its own. Pipelines and cargoes do that.

parts.name: Gas day balance
parts.detail: Today's demand versus the level that would trigger a National Gas margins notice.

parts.name: Power spare
parts.detail: Tightest day in the next fortnight is 2026-11-06: forecast national demand 38.6 GW, spare generation 6.6 GW, so the peak uses 85% of what NESO is counting as available. Live demand at 2026-10-29T08:40:00Z was 34.2 GW. Night demand is not the tight moment.

shelf.note: Online catalogues, not the shop on your street. Trolley shows which supermarkets currently publish a price for the same product. Morrisons reports an available flag. Tesco, Asda and Sainsbury's block direct checks. If Ocado blocks the read, that is a block, not an empty shelf.

method: Pump prices are the DESNZ weekly series from 2018. Stress is their percentile in that history, plus a kick if the last four weeks rose.
Brent, Dutch TTF gas and Chicago wheat are daily futures from Yahoo, scored on their own two-year percentile and 30-day change.
Weather stress is the last 45 days of rain and temperature versus the same calendar window in the previous ten years, from Open-Meteo.

This harvest uses the AHDB final 2026 survey against the five-year yield average, not the change versus last year. Defra's England tonnage is shown beside it and is not allowed to cancel the yield gap.
Fruit and meat standing scores do not move daily. They are the structural exposure from the UK Food Security Report, not a live shock.

Eggs, milk, bread and chicken are read from public Ocado and Morrisons search pages, plus a Trolley price comparison for Tesco, Asda and Sainsbury's. That is an online catalogue, not your local shelf. A score of 0 means every listed shell egg was marked available.
Emergency oil stocks are DESNZ Energy Trends table 3.11. The score stays in Watch while the last quarterly note says the IEA 90-day test is met, even if the tonne total is low for the decade.
Fuel in the depot is table 3.11 stocks divided by table 3.13 deliveries in the same month. It is not the emergency reserve.
Gas in store and the gas-day balance come from National Gas. Medium-range fill is the storage score. Long-range is shown and not treated as a buffer when it is published at zero.
Power spare is the smallest NESO surplus over the next fortnight, set against that day's demand forecast from Elexon. It is spare generation, not a map of weak points.
